expectations.text: Output warns that aggregating to a static graph loses temporal information and conflates different time periods
expectations.evidence: When you collapse 2.3M timestamped emails into a single weighted adjacency matrix... you lose at minimum: Causal ordering... Conflation of different time periods. Three years of email is not one network — it is an evolving sequence. An employee who was a connector in year 1 and left in year 2 looks the same as one who was a connector in all three years.

expectations.text: Output mentions time-respecting paths (temporal paths that respect arrow of time) as a key concept — and explains that paths in the aggregate can be causally impossible if timestamps are out of order
expectations.evidence: The concept that captures this is time-respecting paths: a sequence of contacts i→x₁ at t₁, x₁→x₂ at t₂, … where t₁ < t₂ < … < tₖ. These are the only paths by which a piece of information sent at t₁ can propagate. Your aggregate graph will contain paths that violate this constraint... Paths that look valid in the aggregated graph can be causally impossible if the timestamps are out of order.

expectations.text: Output recommends temporal network analysis tools (pathpy, teneto, snap-temporal, or equivalent)
expectations.evidence: Recommended workflow: Run temporal network analysis directly on the event sequence using pathpy (Python, Scholtes et al.) or teneto (Python, Thompson). Both compute time-respecting path statistics and temporal centrality. Code example using pathpy is also provided.

expectations.text: Output explains that static betweenness and temporal betweenness can rank nodes in qualitatively different orders, not just quantitatively
expectations.evidence: These two metrics can rank nodes in qualitatively different orders, not just different magnitudes. An employee who sits on many shortest paths in the static graph may not sit on many time-respecting paths... Conversely, an employee who looks low-centrality in the static graph may be a consistently available bridge at just the right times. The reversal is not hypothetical; it is well-documented in empirical temporal network studies.

expectations.text: Output does NOT simply validate the static-aggregation plan as sufficient for understanding communication dynamics
expectations.evidence: Your static aggregation plan will produce rankings that are wrong in a systematic way... The aggregate approach is not sufficient for understanding communication dynamics; it answers a simpler and different question.
